The cover text: the Irish above (two sentences changed from the last brief: cainteoir Gaeilge ort sa chomhrá; Faoin chéad chomhrá eile) and its English line for line, the rubrics (Do chomhrá, scríofa agat roimh ré; Gach a ndéarfaidh tú sa chomhrá; Cé thú féin agus cá huair a bheas an chéad chomhrá eile; Comhrá gan scríbhinn; Cúig cheist and Trí cheist, gan do scríbhinn os do chomhair; Gan iarraidh go fóill), the item instructions (Abairt amháin; Abairt amháin, le ham nó áit; Dhá abairt, agus cad chuige; Freagra iomlán; Scríobh í sa diúltach; Scríobh í mar cheist; Scríobh í mar a bhí inné; mar a bheas amárach; Ceist ar ais; Abair í, ansin éist leat féin; Éist agus amharc) and the pen phrases (fada!; séimhiú de dhíth; urú de dhíth; X de dhíth; agat, ní agam; An bhfuil de dhíth; cad chuige?; bheith ag; ceartaithe; maith thú; Sin é anocht; gan dáta go fóill). Claude drafts in Ulster Irish, Dáithí signs off. Size: about 45 strings plus the two cover paragraphs.

A verb paradigm table for the Foirm turn and the Marker's inflection stop list: for the verbs a pupil uses first (tá, bí, déan, téigh, tar, imir, ith, ól, éirigh, amharc, éist, faigh, feic, labhair, tosaigh, críochnaigh, caith, ceannaigh, cuidigh, réitigh) the first-person present, past and future, and the positive, negative and interrogative rows in each tense, keyed to the 69 listed verb rows (which already carry ní bhíonn, An mbíonn, ní dhearna, ní fhaca, ní dheachaigh, ndearna, ndeachaigh, bhfaca); the person shift pairs (agam/agat, liom/leat, orm/ort, dom/duit, mo/do). Claude drafts, Dáithí signs off. Size: 20 verbs by about 9 forms, roughly 180 forms, plus 5 pairs.

vocab.json cleaning at load or in the workbook: drop the 29 legend rows K0798 to K0826; drop the duplicates K0717 dúinn, K0767 siopa, K0517 pointe, K0777 turas, K0711 mall, K0726 ceathrar; collapse the níos rows (K0050, K0079, K0152, K0363) to one; correct K0750 deirfiúir to deirfiúr; add orainn to the ar paradigm; decide whether gaol (n mpl) and éadaí (n mpl) stand as headwords. Claude does the load-time rules; Dáithí signs off the two spelling and headword decisions. Size: about 40 rows.

A school supplement to the frequency list with gender and part of speech for words a Year 8 line needs that the list lacks: on the topic list without gender (mamaí, guthán, éide scoile, club, eitleán, deirfiúr as a second spelling, buachaill, cistin, staighre, snámh, dochtúir, deoch, torthaí, glasraí, and the colours gorm, glas, buí, donn, fionn, and the adjectives suimiúil, greannmhar, leadránach) and on neither list (daidí, cineálta, cairdiúil, fliuch, tinn, brónach, go raibh maith agat, cionn is, as siocair, Cáisc, laethanta saoire). Until it exists these words are recognised for the fada and the index by fold only and never for mutation. Claude drafts, Dáithí signs off. Size: about 35 rows. The personal numerals (beirt K0284, triúr K0395, ceathrar K0656, cúigear K0748, seisear K0727, seachtar K0728, ochtar K0729, naonúr K0730, deichniúr K0780), gruaig K0755, súil K0148, the weather adjectives and the months are already listed and need nothing.

The reason-word list for the Year 10 line and the cad chuige? check: mar and mar gheall ar are listed (K0026, K0039, K0197); cionn is, as siocair, de bhrí, óir and toisc are not on either list. Dáithí confirms which Ulster forms count. Size: 7 strings.

The topic list's gender cleaned in the workbook (827 of its 2,233 rows are marked m and none f) before it can ever feed the mutation note; until then the article drill runs only on the 349 frequency-list nouns with pos n (m) or n (f). Dáithí's department cleans; Claude imports. Size: 827 rows to check, or the 60 or so a Year 8 and Year 9 meet first.

The marking hand: an apostrophe and capital fadas digitised from the photographed sample sheet, since s'againne, d'éide and D'ith appear in lines and pen notes. Dáithí photographs the sheet; Claude digitises. Size: about 12 glyphs.

The printed conversation card layout: candidate box, hand line, question column for the speaker, the pupil's line, a blank rule and a tick box per line, on A4 through ImageRenderer. Claude drafts, Dáithí signs off the page. Size: one template.
Atkinson Hyperlegible bundled for every print face. Claude. Size: one font family.

No audio files. The Abair integration point specified as a play control before the print on the Abair é item and the cold-exam screen only, with no other screen moving. Claude documents in README. Size: one paragraph.
openQuestions: Will the department commit to one conversation per class each half term for Years 8 to 10, and who holds it (the class teacher with the printed card in an Irish lesson, Year 12 partners under supervision, a visiting speaker, the Gaeltacht), and which two pages are fixed for Year 8 and Year 9 and which six offered to Year 10? Without a date the Year 8 cell reads gan dáta go fóill and the thread is as empty as the narrowing that was rejected.
Does the department write t before s for masculine nouns after a preposition and the article (ag an tsiopa) or leave it (ag an siopa)? The pen accepts both until ruled.

critiques.lens: A 12-year-old in 8B, three weeks into Irish, never sat an exam, has an iPhone. I know about forty words. I care about two things: do I understand what this booklet is for, and does it feel like mine or like something borrowed from the Year 12s.
critiques.verdict: I understand what it is for. "Write what you will say in your next conversation, one line a night" is a sentence I can repeat to my mum, and the cell on the cover that says Comhrá: Bliain 12, 14 Samhain is the best thing in the brief: a real person from Year 12 is going to sit across from me with my own printed sheet as their card and ask me my questions. That is a reason to write a line tonight that no exam in 2031 could give me. But the booklet does not yet feel like mine, because the data says it runs out on me. Night one takes 7 of the 11 one-sentence questions on the Myself page (Q001 to Q007 are all tier 1); after that my two fixed pages hold at most 19 more tier-1 questions (Myself 4 left, School 15; Free time would give 20), so Líne nua goes grey about four weeks after I start and stays grey until Year 9. The walkthrough already knows this: Caoimhe's line 8 on sheet 1a is Q039 from the Free time page, which is not on her two pages and not on any sheet cut by question number. Beyond that, three of the four nightly items lean on things a Year 8 line does not contain (preposition plus article plus gendered noun for Foirm; a listed word missing from a rewrite; a line I have heard said, for Abair é), and the seven-question first night, the twenty-second wait and a page titled Mo chuid botún in the Principal's red are the places a pupil like me with ADHD puts the phone down. The thread holds for every year only if the Year 8 booklet is cut for a Year 8: the tier-1 pool across all twelve pages as its own sheets, the sheet as a view over lines keyed by question id, and the exam's skeleton (grey pages, grey lines, countdown, pace) kept out of sight until the year that needs it.

problems.problem: The Year 8 runs out of new lines in a month. Counting the first-pass tiers against questions.json: Myself has 11 tier-1 questions of 21, School 15 of 33, Free time 20 of 39, Local area 13 of 36, and Travel and Future plans have none. Night one uses Q001 to Q007. With two fixed pages a Year 8 has 19 to 24 tier-1 questions left, one a night, then item 4 has no candidate for the remaining thirty weeks and the candidate box reads Líne 10 de 10 with nothing that fills. The brief's own walkthrough breaks its rule to hide this: Caoimhe's sheet 1a line 8 is Q039, a Free time question, not on her two pages.
problems.fix: For Years 8 and 9 the pool is every question at the year's tier on every page (95 tier-1 questions, of which about 80 need no travel or workplace), not two pages. Cut that pool into Year 8 sheets of ten in an order the department signs (sheet 1: Q001 to Q007, Q009, Q010, Q039; sheet 2: home and school; and so on), so a sheet fills inside a fortnight and there are eight or nine sheets, a school year of nights. The 'two pages' rule starts in Year 10 when pages are chosen. A sheet is a view over lines keyed by question id, so Caoimhe's Q004 line is the same line Aoife crosses through in Year 11; line references print as page.line of the exam cut only from Year 11, and as sheet.line of the year's cut before that.

problems.problem: The first night is seven blank rules on one screen, which is seven things per screen on the night the ADHD ruling says one. Three weeks in I cannot write 'Tá cúigear sa teaghlach' (Q003) or 'i mBéal Feirste' (Q002) without help, there are no model answers, and the only help (the opener) arrives after twenty seconds of staring at a blank line. Seven waits of twenty seconds is the first experience of the app.
problems.fix: Night one is four lines I already own, copied from the cover: Q001 from Ainm, Q002 from the townland locative, Q006 from the school's name, Q007 from Rang. The rules carry the opener printed in grey at once (Tá mé i mo chónaí i ...) and the pupil writes over it in biro; the pen marks fada only. Night two is Q003 to Q005 with the personal numerals (beirt K0284 to deichniúr K0780) offered as the word bank's first row. For Years 8 and 9 the opener is always printed at once and a tap hides it; the twenty-second idle reveal starts in Year 10. That removes the only hidden timer from the year that cannot bear one.

problems.problem: Item 3 Foirm has no candidate on most Year 8 lines. The gap turn needs preposition plus article plus a noun with a gender row; Year 8 lines are 'Tá deartháir amháin agam', 'Is maith liom peil', 'Tá mé i mo chónaí i ...', 'Tá mé i rang 8B', none of which contains sa, ar an or ag an plus a listed noun (and t and s are excluded anyway). The concept brief's rule that an item with no candidate is skipped means the year most in need of the same four items every night is the year that gets three, silently.
problems.fix: For Year 8, Foirm is only two turns that every tá or is line can take, so there is always a candidate: Scríobh í mar cheist (Tá -> An bhfuil, Is maith liom -> An maith leat, Imrím -> An imríonn tú) and Scríobh í sa diúltach (Tá -> Níl, Is maith liom -> Ní maith liom, Imrím -> Ní imrím), both with the person shift pairs agam/agat, liom/leat, orm/ort, dom/duit, mo/do. The gap turn joins in Year 9 and the tense turn from Year 9 as the brief says. The check is the 20-verb paradigm table, not the 69 verb rows in vocab.json, which are a recognition list with imperatives (imir, éirigh, labhair) and scattered finite forms (rinne, ndearna, ní fhaca) and cannot turn a line; the brief names both as the check and should name one.

problems.problem: Abair é from box 2 asks me to say a line from memory that I have never heard anyone say. Ruling 2 keeps the questions in print, and the brief keeps phonics in the classroom, so a Year 8 recording 'deartháir' has no reference and hears back her own guess, then has to mark herself tic or arís on a pronunciation she cannot judge. The paper-to-voice ladder is the half of the box schedule that print-only data cannot deliver before Abair.
problems.fix: Until the Abair play control exists, boxes 2 to 5 for Years 8 and 9 stay Athscríobh (rewrite from memory, marked by the pen) and Abair é is offered under it as an extra with no tic or arís and no effect on the box: record once, hear it back, done. The ladder from paper to voice switches on per year when Abair is wired in, and README says so in the paragraph the brief already promises. Year 11 and 12 keep Abair é gating box 2 because they have heard the lines in class for three years.

problems.problem: Ceist ar ais does not turn anything round. The 270 questions are already addressed to you (Cad é an t-ainm atá ort?, An bhfuil ríomhaire agat?), so 'one printed question turned round to ask the partner' is the same string as the print. A Year 8 will not know what changed and the pen has nothing to check.
problems.fix: Define Ceist ar ais as writing the printed question itself from memory, hidden, so that the pupil can open the conversation and not only answer in it (asking is the Key Stage 3 skill the answers never drill). The pen marks fada and a listed word missing, as in Athscríobh. Once per sheet, item 4, and on the printed card that line prints in the pupil's column with the partner's answer rule blank.

problems.problem: Ten of twelve pages are grey and on my own pages half the lines are grey 'not yet asked' for four years. That is the Year 12 exam booklet showing through mine; a grey page I cannot touch until 2030 tells a 12-year-old the app belongs to the big ones. The cold exam screen with 'the only countdown' and the inside cover's five years of empty conversation rows say the same thing.
problems.fix: An scríbhinn in Years 8 to 10 lists only the year's sheets, none grey; the twelve exam pages appear when the pupil chooses them in Year 10. Grey lines at the foot of a sheet are dropped for Years 8 and 9 (the next tier's questions arrive as new sheets next year, on the same page in the data). Comhrá gan scríbhinn has no countdown in Years 8 to 10; the countdown and the Scrúdú béil rubric arrive with the exam date in Year 11. The inside cover shows past conversation rows and the next one, and adds a row when the department sets a date.

problems.problem: The next conversation can be blank, and then the sentence the app is built on has no object. The date is typed by the pupil from the board; if the teacher has not written it, the cell reads 'gan dáta go fóill' and a Year 8's booklet is a script for a conversation that is not happening. Also Q006 cannot be answered until the school's name in Irish exists in departmentPages.json, and Q002 needs the townland as said after i, which is the eclipsis a three-week Year 8 cannot produce; the cover asks the pupil to supply it.
problems.fix: Ship a default calendar per class: partner an múinteoir on the last school night of each half term, and for Year 8 the first conversation is Bliain 12 in the first half term (the hook that makes the booklet real), replaced when the board says otherwise; the cell is never blank. departmentPages.json carries the school's name and a signed catchment table of about thirty townlands with name and locative (An Sruthán, i mBéal Feirste style), so the cover offers the locative from a list and the pupil types only if theirs is missing.

problems.problem: The pen writes in Irish I cannot read yet. 'amháin de dhíth', 'agat, ní agam', 'séimhiú de dhíth' carry no English, and the cover's 'Ceartóidh an peann dearg na fadaí, an séimhiú agus an t-urú' names three things a Year 8 three weeks in has not met in English either. The rubrics get English beneath; the pen and the item instructions (Scríobh í mar cheist, Athscríobh ó chuimhne) do not.
problems.fix: Every pen phrase and item instruction carries a one-line grey English gloss beneath for Years 8 and 9 (fada! / fada missing; amháin de dhíth / amháin is missing; agat, ní agam / you, not me), as the concept brief's build step 4 already had for the rule gloss; the gloss goes from Year 10 or on a tap. The cover's English first line settles the sense of scríbhinn for a Year 8 as the lines you will say, not an exam script: 'This is your own script: what you will say.'

problems.problem: Mo chuid botún is a page of my mistakes in the Principal's red hand that only grows. For a pupil with ADHD who already believes they are bad at this, it is the page never opened, and the Innéacs puts it last where it looks like the verdict on the booklet.
problems.fix: Name it for what it does, Le ceartú, keep at most five entries visible (the ones due to be retested), and drop an entry the night it is written right rather than after three nights and crossed through. The stamp's kind line already names the thing fixed (deartháir ceartaithe); that is the record a Year 8 should see, not the ledger.

problems.problem: Priontáil hides a round trip a Year 8 cannot do. The teacher's correction and the partner's card both depend on a PDF from ImageRenderer leaving the phone: I have no printer, so the sheet has to be shared to the teacher, marked on paper, and the correction typed back in by me. Nothing in the brief names the share, and the walkthrough gives Caoimhe a correction typed in as if the paper came back on its own.
problems.fix: The foot action is Seol chuig an mhúinteoir, the iOS share sheet with the PDF attached and the teacher's address remembered from the cover; Priontáil is the same action on a Mac or a school iPad. The class conversation date is the day sheets are collected, so the brief's 'one printed sheet back' has a day it happens. Ceartú an mhúinteora is where the pupil types what came back.

problems.problem: Rang drives the tier but the pupil cannot see the tier. The cover cell is 'Rang (8 to 12)', the walkthrough writes 8B and 11B, and the year has to be parsed from that. The item instruction (Abairt amháin) is the only visible sign of what the year asks, and nothing on the cover says that typing 11 would change what the pen writes.
problems.fix: Two cells: Bliain as a picker 8 to 12 and Rang as free text (8B). Under Bliain the cover prints the year's rule in one line (I mBliain 8: abairt amháin; I mBliain 10: dhá abairt, agus cad chuige), so the grade of a line is stated where the year is set and a Year 8 sees what next year will ask.

problems.problem: Feels like mine until the phone changes. One Script file in the Documents folder, no server, means the booklet from Year 8 is gone the day the phone is replaced or reset, and Glan on the cover with a friend holding my phone loses five years in one tap.
problems.fix: Store the Script file in the app's iCloud Drive container so it follows the Apple ID, and offer Cóip a shábháil (export the JSON and the full PDF through the share sheet) from the cover at every conversation date. Glan asks the pupil to type their Ainm before it runs and clears only the current year's unfinished lines; earlier years' crossed-through lines stay, because they are the point of the five-year booklet.

critiques.stillMissing: Data the Year 8 booklet needs beyond the brief's list: a Year 8 sheet order over the tier-1 pool across all twelve pages (about 80 questions once travel and workplace ones are set aside), signed by the department, since the two-page rule gives a Year 8 only 19 to 24 questions; the tier of Q011 and Q012 (comparatives is sine, níos sine) rechecked, as they are tier 1 by the first pass but not a three-week sentence; a catchment townland table with locatives (about 30 rows) so Q002 and the cover can be filled without eclipsis knowledge; the English gloss strings for the pen phrases and item instructions (about 25) in addition to the 45 Irish strings; a default conversation calendar with Bliain 12 as the Year 8 first partner; the vocab supplement rows the first nights hit at once (deirfiúr as headword, mamaí, daidí, guthán, dúil for Q058, greannmhar, suimiúil), which are on the brief's list but should be sequenced first; and a ruling on whether a Year 8 sheet is Críochnaithe when every line at its tier is written, which decides whether the progress object ever fills.

critiques.lens: Head of Irish running the scheme across Years 8 to 12: must meet the Key Stage 3 framework from 2028 in Years 8 to 10 and still get Year 12 through the speaking exam, with one department, one print run and one data file per pupil. Judged against the data as it stands: questions.json (270 rows, id, ga, topic, context only), vocab.json (826 ks3 rows: 349 nouns with gender, 69 verb rows, 29 legend rows; 2,233 gcse rows, 827 marked m and none f), CONCEPT.md and PROPOSAL.md sections 10 to 12.
critiques.verdict: The screens are one scheme: the same six pages, four items, pen, boxes and printed card serve every year, and the year differences are gates, not forks. The data underneath is two half-schemes joined at the seam. The spine of the app is the 270 exam questions, which are a Year 11 and 12 artefact: on any two pages a Year 8 has 24 to 31 tier-1 questions and runs out of new lines in the first five to six weeks of a 190-night year, after which the "object that fills" stops filling; the frequency list, which is what the Key Stage 3 framework actually asks for, appears in only 229 of its 797 content headwords across all 270 questions, so the Focal item can never reach the other 568. The five-year thread holds only if the department's Year 8 to 10 pages are the pages the same pupil later chooses for the exam, and only if the one Script file survives four device changes, and the brief provides for neither. The grade-follows-year rule collapses on factual questions, as the brief's own Aoife example shows (a Year 11 rewriting Tá deartháir amháin agam). Print-only is handled honestly except in two places: the cover promises séimhiú and urú correction that the gender-gated rule cannot give a Year 8, and box advancement from box 2 rests on a self-marked tic the pen cannot check. Every break has a fix inside the existing shape; none needs a new screen. Workable as one scheme once the items below are settled, and Dáithí's page choice for Years 8 to 10 is the decision that makes or breaks the thread.

problems.problem: The Year 8 pool is exhausted in October. Tier-1 questions per topic (first pass, verified against questions.json): Free time 20, School 15, Local area 13, Myself 11, Social media 10, Social issues 8, Part-time 6, Culture 5, Extra-curricular 5, Community 2, Travel 0, Future plans 0. Two fixed pages give 24 to 31 distinct tier-1 lines (Myself and School: 26, of which Q006/Q191 and Q007/Q192 are the same question twice). Night one writes seven of them together. At one line a night the Líne nua item has no candidate from about the sixth week, and the brief's own rule (an item with no candidate is skipped) means Anocht is three rewrite items for the remaining 160 nights. Year 9 on the same two pages at tier 2 adds only 21 (Myself 9, School 12); Year 10 on the same pages at tier 3 adds 7. The promise "until nothing is new" is met in Year 8 by half term, and the sheet, the one object the ADHD section says must fill inside a fortnight, has nothing to fill after the third sheet.
problems.fix: Two changes, no new screen. (1) Make the sheet fill four times, not once, so rewrites are visible progress: a sheet carries four stamps in the hand, scríofa (every rule in biro), athscríofa (every line rewritten from memory once right), ráite (every line said aloud from box 2), and ticeáilte (every line ticked on the printed card at the conversation). The candidate box reads the current fill: Líne 5 de 10, athscríofa 3 de 10. Críochnaithe only after the fourth. (2) Put pages on the half-term calendar the brief already has for conversation dates: a department page per half term, not two per year. Concretely, Year 8: Myself and School in half terms 1 to 3 (24 lines), Free time in 4 to 6 (20 lines), 44 new lines a year; Year 9: the same three at tier 2 (36) plus Local area at tiers 1 and 2 (31), 67 lines; Year 10: tier 3 on those four (16) plus one new page from the six at tiers 1 to 3. The tier counts above are the arithmetic the department needs to see before it fixes the pages.

problems.problem: The five-year thread exists only if the pages coincide. "A Year 8 line stays under the Year 12 answer" is true only when the Year 11 pupil's two chosen pages (from twelve) are pages written in Years 8 to 10. With Year 8 and 9 pages fixed by the department and Year 11 pages free, the coincidence is at most partial, and a pupil who chooses Travel and Part-time (0 and 6 tier-1 questions, 16 of the 36 gcseOnly rows) arrives in Year 11 with a blank booklet and four years of lines on pages the exam never touches. The brief says the exam is on two chosen topics; nothing in it ties the department's Year 8 to 10 choice to the exam choice.
problems.fix: State the rule in departmentPages.json rather than hoping: the Year 8 to 10 pages are the pages the department expects most candidates to choose in Year 11 (on the tier counts, Myself, School, Free time, Local area), and a Year 11 who chooses a page outside those four sees, on the cover, the count of lines already written on each page before choosing (Saol na scoile: 31 líne scríofa; Taisteal: 0). The thread is then a property of the data the pupil can see, not of luck. Nothing else changes.

problems.problem: One Script file across five years, no server, on a device the pupil will not keep for five years. The brief keeps the CONCEPT's JSON in the Documents folder. A Year 8 iPad is reassigned; a phone is replaced; a pupil moves from a school device to their own. Any of these ends the booklet. Priontáil an scríbhinn ar fad, the only backup, is listed for Year 12 only.
problems.fix: Store the Script JSON in the app's iCloud Documents container so it follows the Apple ID, and add to An clúdach istigh two lines under Glan: Cóip den scríbhinn (share sheet, the JSON) and Oscail cóip (import, replacing after confirmation). Priontáil an scríbhinn ar fad on the cover in every year, since the paper booklet is the backup the department can hold. Size: one container entitlement, two cover actions, one file format already defined.

problems.problem: The grade-follows-year rule fails on factual questions. "One sentence in Year 8, two with a reason word in Year 10, a full answer with an opinion in Year 12" cannot apply to Q004 Cá mhéad deartháir atá agat?, Q009 Cad é an aois thú? or 60 of the 95 tier-1 questions, which have one true answer. The brief's own example proves it: Aoife, Year 11, rewriting 1a.4 as Tá deartháir amháin agam, with her Year 8 line of the same words crossed through beneath. If the machine demands Freagra iomlán from a Year 11 on Q004, the pen either writes nothing (the rule is dead) or writes cad chuige? on a question with no reason (the pen fails its own test). And a new year must not cross through a line the pupil never changed.
problems.fix: Grade is a function of the question's tier and the year, not the year alone: tier-1 questions are Abairt amháin in every year; tier-2 questions are Abairt amháin, le ham nó áit from Year 9; tier-3 questions are grey below Year 10, Dhá abairt, agus cad chuige in Year 10 and Freagra iomlán from Year 11. The item instruction is drawn from that table. A line is crossed through and dated only when the pupil writes a new draft, never on a change of year. Rewrite the Aoife example so item 1 is a tier-2 or tier-3 line.

problems.problem: "Only questions at the year's tier" is ambiguous and both readings break something. Read as "at that tier only", Year 10 on two pages gets between 1 and 6 tier-3 questions (Myself 1, Community 1, Part-time 1; School 6), a year's new work in a week. Read as "at or below", a Year 9 whose pages differ from Year 8's is asked tier-1 questions at Year 9's instruction (with a time or place phrase) that it does not fit, and the Year 8 who moves to Year 9 pages reopens sheets already Críochnaithe.
problems.fix: Write it as "at or below the year's tier", and define a sheet as a page cut by tier, not by count: 1a, 1b are the page's tier-1 questions in sheets of ten; 1c, 1d its tier-2; 1e its tier-3. A finished sheet stays finished; a new year opens the next cut on the same page. The sheet cuts in the twelve-row topic table then fall out of the tier field rather than being authored separately (Free time: 20, 15, 4 gives sheets of 10, 10, 10, 5, 4; Local area 13, 18, 5).

problems.problem: The Key Stage 3 vocabulary strand is not delivered by the questions. By folded and mutation-stripped match, 229 of the 797 content headwords in the ks3 stage appear anywhere in the 270 questions. The Focal item draws only from the next question's listed words, so a Year 8 can meet at most those 229 through Focal, and none of the 17 content words in Na 100 focal is coitianta unless they happen to sit in a question. The framework's spine is the frequency list; the app's spine is the exam's questions. This is the seam where it is two schemes.
problems.fix: Give Focal a third source for Years 8 to 10 without changing the item: (a) a word missed in item 1, else (b) a listed word in the next question, else (c) the next unused headword in band order (Na 100, then 101 go 250, then 251 go 500) with pos in n (m), n (f), adj, v or vn, in the pupil's own sentence. The bands exist in vocab.json as group; the content-word counts are 17, 50, 66, 131, 200 and 88, so a Year 8 covers the first three bands (133 words) in a year at one a night. From Year 11 source (c) is off. The Innéacs shows band-sourced words under the sheet whose night they were written on. Also: the folded match does not handle plurals, so cluichí (Q024, Q046, both tier 1) never matches K0331 cluiche and Q024 yields only ríomhaire; add a plural column to the supplement or a stem rule (strip í, anna, a) for the 349 nouns.

problems.problem: The cover promises what the mutation rule cannot give a Year 8. Ceartóidh an peann dearg na fadaí, an séimhiú agus an t-urú, but the note fires only where preposition and article meet one of the 349 gendered nouns, never on d, t or s. A Year 8 line's mutations are elsewhere: mo/do before a noun (mo mháthair, mo dheartháir, mo theach, mo sheomra), i before a placename (i mBéal Feirste, i nDroim Intí), the school's name after i. In the brief's own Caoimhe example the likely error is mo dearthair, which the pen cannot mark, and the "never on d, t or s" exception, correct after the article, would suppress mo dheartháir and mo theach if applied globally.
problems.fix: Add two gender-free rules to the Marker, since they need no data the topic list lacks: mo, do and a (his) followed by b, c, d, f, g, m, p, s or t without h writes séimhiú de dhíth; i followed by b, c, d, f, g, p or t without the eclipsing letter writes urú de dhíth (in before a vowel accepted). Scope "never on d, t or s" to the article rule only. The cover sentence is then true for a Year 8 on the first night. The townland strings on the cover (as said after Tá mé i mo chónaí) give the machine the correct eclipsed form for Q002 and Q087 without a rule.

problems.problem: Box advancement past 2 rests on a tic the pen cannot check. From box 2 the recall is Abair é: line hidden, recorded, played back against the revealed line, tic or arís by the pupil. There is no reference sound until Abair and no listener. For Years 8 to 10 that is the majority of a line's life in the boxes (2, 4, 8, 16 days) advanced on self-report, against the brief's own test (the pen writes only what a teacher could check). A pupil with ADHD will tic. The CONCEPT's gate (no box past 2 until the sheet is printed) is not listed as removed and would stall every Year 8 who never prints at home.
problems.fix: Until Abair: Abair é is unmarked rehearsal (record, hear, no box change), and boxes 3 to 5 are reached only by the two checkable events: Athscríobh right at box 2 and 3 (the machine), and the partner's or teacher's tick copied from the printed card (see the next item). After Abair, the playback comparison stands in for the tick. Replace the print gate with the card gate: no box past 3 without a tick from a real conversation. This is one line in the box rule and it makes the conversation date do something.

problems.problem: For Years 8 to 10 the real conversation is invisible to the app. The date on the cover is the next conversation with a fluent speaker; the card is printed; the partner ticks boxes on paper; the date passes; nothing in the Script changes. The only return leg is Ceartú an mhúinteora, typed per line, which a Year 8 will not do for a Year 12 partner's ticks. So the one framework requirement that gives the Key Stage 3 years their purpose has no data path, and the date cell is decoration.
problems.fix: On the first night after a conversation date, item 1 is An comhrá instead of Ó chuimhne: the printed card's lines with a tick box each, in print, the pupil copying the partner's ticks from the paper (the input is a copy of a checkable mark, not a judgement). Ticked lines move to box 3; unticked to box 0 and to the head of the queue. That completes the sheet's fourth stamp (ticeáilte) and sets the next date from the calendar. For Years 11 and 12 the same item follows a mock. Size: one item variant, one tick per line, no new Irish beyond An comhrá and Cé a bhí leat?.

problems.problem: Night one is seven blank rules for a pupil with ADHD and no Irish. Every year writes Q001 to Q007 together on night one; there are no model answers, and the opener appears only after twenty seconds idle. For a Year 8 in September that is seven Irish sentences to compose at once on the first open, the opposite of one thing per screen, and twenty seconds of a blank rule is longer than the attention the section 10 fork allows. The cover already holds the words for four of the seven (name, townland as said, school name, class).
problems.fix: Night one in Year 8 is Líon an bhearna on one rule at a time: Q001, Q002, Q006 and Q007 prefilled in grey from the cover (Is mise ___; Tá mé i mo chónaí i ___; Tá mé ar scoil i ___; Tá mé i Rang ___), copied in biro as the first Athscríobh; Q003 to Q005 as frames with the number blank (Tá ___ duine i mo theaghlach; Tá ___ deartháir agam), the personal numerals K0284 to K0780 and amháin the word bank's first row that night. The opener delay is 0 seconds in Years 8 and 9 and 20 from Year 10. Item instruction Líon an bhearna is one new string for sign-off. From night two, Abairt amháin as written.

problems.problem: The Foirm turn has no verb data and no copula. "Made negative, made a question with the person shifted, or from Year 9 put in another tense, checked against the 69 listed verb forms": the 69 rows are a bag of forms (bhí, tá, rinne, chuaigh, ní bhíonn, An mbíonn, caithfidh, tugann), not paradigms, and the brief's own 20-verb table is still to be drafted and signed. Until it is signed Foirm has no candidate for most Year 8 lines and every night is three items. The 20 verbs omit the copula, yet 12 of the 95 tier-1 questions are answered with is maith liom or is fearr liom (Q039 to Q041, Q044, Q080, Q081, Q095, Q100, Q112, Q182, Q184, Q200) and the negative and question turns of those are ní maith liom and an maith leat, and the tense turn on tá lines (Tá deartháir agam to Bhí deartháir agam) is nonsense.
problems.fix: Add is (copula) to the table: is, ní, an; ba, níor, ar; with the liom/leat shift, and tá already listed. Restrict the tense turn to lines whose verb is in the table and is not tá or is, and prefer the six tense questions: a Year 9's present-tense line on part b of Q051, Q056, Q063, Q066, Q071 or Q077 is turned into parts a and c, so the 18 part rows do double duty as Foirm keys and the turn never leaves the question set. Until the table is signed, Foirm offers only the gap (sa ______ (carr)) and the mo/do and i rules above, which need no paradigm.

problems.problem: Four questions are printed twice and would be written, queued and examined twice: Q002 = Q087, Q006 = Q191, Q007 = Q192, Q067 = Q194 (exact matches in questions.json), with Q204 and Q218, Q020 and Q049, Q070 and Q203 near enough that a Year 8 on Myself and School writes the same line on two sheets and Athscríobh drills both.
problems.fix: A sameAs field on the second row of each pair; the second prints in grey with a line reference (féach 1a.6), shares the line and its boxes, and counts once for the cold screen and the pace. Four ids, one field, no Irish.

problems.problem: Tier 1 is question shape, not year fit. Among the 95 tier-1 questions are Q223 An bhfuil post páirtaimseartha agat? (a Year 8 cannot legally have one; the line is Níl), Q142 An mbíonn fadhbanna sóisialta i do cheantar?, Q034 Cad é an cineál teicneolaíochta a úsáideann tú?, Q135 Cad é an cineál bia a itheann tú le tú féin a choinneáil sláintiúil?, Q249 An bhfuil cuntas bainc agat?, Q010 Cad é dáta do lá breithe? (months and ordinals before a Year 8 has them). A fluent speaker does not ask an 11-year-old these; the framework wants a real conversation, and the page fixed by the department could put six such lines on a Year 8 sheet.
problems.fix: Keep tier as shape and add a fromYear floor on the few rows that need it (draft: Q223, Q244 to Q249 at 9; Q142, Q135, Q137, Q140, Q148, Q034 at 9; Q010 at 9), so a tier-1 question below its floor sits grey at the sheet's foot as the brief already does for higher tiers. About 12 judgements for Dáithí, no new Irish.

problems.problem: The teacher's correction leg does not scale to five year groups. Every sheet is printed, corrected by the teacher, and the correction typed in by the pupil. Twenty classes of 25 with a sheet each fortnight is 500 A4 pages a fortnight for a department of a few teachers, and a Year 8 printing at home is the least likely link in the chain. The le seiceáil state and Priontáil an leathanach when five unprinted lines exist assume a printer in every house.
problems.fix: One print per pupil per half term, and it is the card: the sheet printed for the conversation is the sheet the teacher corrects, with the partner's tick column and the teacher's correction rule on the same A4. Priontáil an leathanach becomes Seol an leathanach (share sheet to the teacher, who prints in class) with the flag tugtha isteach; Priontáil stays as a second choice. For Years 11 and 12 the department may set two prints a half term. The template stays one.

problems.problem: Two names for one screen name the exam in the Key Stage 3 years' favour and overpromise in Year 12's. Screen 5 is Comhrá gan scríbhinn for 8 to 10 and Scrúdú béil for 11 and 12, yet in both the pupil reads a printed question and speaks into a recorder; there is no examiner's voice until Abair. CONCEPT.md ruled never to claim likeness to the day until audio exists; calling the screen Scrúdú béil does exactly that in print.
problems.fix: One rubric for every year, Comhrá gan scríbhinn, with the count varying (Trí cheist, Cúig cheist); Scrúdú béil appears on the screen only when the Abair play control is live. The candidate box already says Scrúdú: Bealtaine 2028 for 11 and 12, which is enough.

problems.problem: The date cell will read gan dáta go fóill for most Year 8s. The conversation date is written on the board and typed by pupils; a pupil with ADHD does not copy the board. The anchor of every screen (the date the script is for) is then empty for the year group that most needs it.
problems.fix: Ship the default the brief already proposes (an múinteoir at the end of each half term) as dates in departmentPages.json per year group, so the cell is never empty; the board's date replaces it when typed. The six partner labels and six dates a year are the department's, encoded once.

problems.problem: Typing fadas is the commonest friction and the commonest pen note. Every fada! costs an ADHD pupil a long-press hunt per vowel, and Ceartúcháin retypes the whole form; Caoimhe's night in the brief has two fada corrections in four items.
problems.fix: An input accessory row above the keyboard with á é í ó ú (and the apostrophe the marking hand needs), on every rule. It supplies keys, not answers; the pupil still chooses the vowel. One view, no Irish.

critiques.stillMissing: Beyond the brief's own data list, which checks out against the files (95, 33 and 36 ids verified disjoint; 42 slash rows, six of them tense; 349 gendered nouns; 69 verb rows; 29 legend rows K0798 to K0826; 827 m and 0 f on the topic list), these are needed before the scheme is one scheme: (1) a department decision on the Year 8 to 10 pages made against the tier counts per topic, with a page per half term rather than two a year; (2) a fromYear floor on about 12 tier-1 questions; (3) sameAs on Q087, Q191, Q192 and Q194; (4) the copula rows in the verb table and a plural column (or stem rule) for the 349 nouns; (5) the mo/do and i mutation rules, gender-free, in the Marker; (6) the An comhrá item and the four-stamp sheet in the Script model, with the box rule tied to the card tick rather than to printing; (7) iCloud container plus export and import on the cover; (8) the band-order third source for Focal in Years 8 to 10; (9) the half-term dates as defaults in departmentPages.json; (10) Líon an bhearna and An comhrá as two more strings for sign-off. Unverifiable from the files: whether Year 8 pupils in the school have iOS devices at home, and how many Irish teachers the department has, both of which set whether the print leg and the partner rota can be run at all.

critiques.lens: Product designer: rejects the generic and anything that is two apps stapled; wants one idea running through every screen for every year, 8 to 12.
critiques.verdict: The rewrite has found the right single object: one booklet whose sheets reopen as the pupil grows, with the printed card as the one thing that binds a Year 8's teacher conversation to a Year 12's examiner. That is not two apps. But the thread is asserted, not yet engineered: the sheet cut is undefined for Years 8 to 10 and the brief's own Caoimhe example contradicts it (she is on sheet 1a, Líne 8 de 10, writing Q039, which is a Free time question on page 3); the tier gating leaves a Year 8 with at most 35 new questions across two pages (Free time 20 plus School 15, minus duplicates and the seven written on night one), so Líne nua runs dry by October and the promised four items collapse to three for the rest of the year; two of the four nightly items (the negative turn and the question turn) have no key the pen can defend; and "a Year 8 line stays under the Year 12 answer" is only true if the Year 12 happens to choose the Year 8 page. Each of these has a fix inside the same idea. The thread holds if the sheet is defined once by page and question order, the tier decides which rules are live, a finished sheet reopens rather than closes, page 1 never closes, and item 4 has something honest to do when the pages are written out.

problems.problem: The sheet cut is not defined for Years 8 to 10 and the brief contradicts itself. Year 8 has sheets of ten, Year 9 of twelve, Year 11 of ten to twenty, yet both worked examples cite 1a.4 as Q004 (the same reference), and Caoimhe (8B) on sheet 1a, Líne 8 de 10, writes Q039, which sits on the Free time page, not on sheet 1a of Myself. On the Myself page (21 questions) only 11 are tier 1 and 9 of them are Q001 to Q011 with Q008 grey; Q013 to Q021 hold two tier 1 questions (Q011, Q012), so a Year 8 sheet 1b of ten questions would have two live rules and Críochnaithe after two nights. The object that fills inside a fortnight fills in two nights on some sheets and never on others.
problems.fix: Cut sheets once, by page and question order, in the twelve-row topic table, the same cut for every year, so 1a.4 is Q004 for Caoimhe and for Aoife. The year's tier decides which rules on that sheet are live; the candidate box counts live rules only (Líne 8 de 9 on 1a in Year 8, since Q008 is grey). Críochnaithe goes across the sheet when every live rule is written, and when Rang rises in September the same sheet reopens with the next tier's rules live and the old Críochnaithe crossed through and dated. Reopening is the one mechanism that already exists (the Year 8 line under the Year 12 answer); make it the definition of a sheet. Drop the per-year sheet sizes.

problems.problem: Líne nua runs dry in the first half term for Years 8 and 10 and the four-item night breaks. Tier 1 by page: Free time 20, School 15 (13 net of Q191, Q192 duplicating Q006, Q007), Local area 13 (12 net of Q087), Myself 11, Social media 10, Social issues 8, Part-time 6, Culture 5, Extra-curricular 5, Community 2, Travel 0, Future 0. The best two fixed pages give 35 tier 1 questions, 28 after night one; on the Myself and School pairing it is 26 minus 3 duplicates minus 7, so 16 new lines for the year. Tier 3 has 33 questions in all: Year 10's two pages from six yield between 2 (Myself 1 plus Part-time 1) and 11 (School 6 plus Local area 5) new lines for the whole year. After that item 4 is skipped and the night has three items, which is the opposite of "the same four items in the same order every night".
problems.fix: Two changes inside the idea. First, the department's fixed pages are chosen with these counts in front of it: Year 8 must be two of Free time, School, Local area, Myself, Social media (the only pages with ten or more tier 1 questions), and Future plans (all 17 gcseOnly) and Travel (0 tier 1) can never be a Year 8 or 9 page. Second, when both open pages have no unasked question at the tier, item 4 becomes Líne níos fearr rather than nothing: the oldest line on the sheet rewritten one grade up (Abairt amháin, le ham nó áit) as a new dated draft under the old one, crossed through. That is the same crossed-through-and-dated mechanism, so the night keeps four items and the booklet keeps filling. Tier questions on the third and fourth pages stay grey; the booklet does not sprawl.

problems.problem: Foirm's negative turn writes lines the pen cannot defend and that are false about the pupil. Tá deartháir amháin agam made negative is Níl deartháir amháin agam, which no teacher would tick (Níl deartháir ar bith agam), and the pen, checking only the listed ní and níl forms, would pass it. Tá mé i mo chónaí i gCamloch made negative is a lie in the pupil's own booklet, in biro; the brief does not say whether Foirm output is saved as a draft.
problems.fix: Restrict the negative turn to lines that answer a yes/no question and turn them the other way (Scríobh an freagra eile): there are 38 such tier 1 questions (Q022, Q023, Q025 to Q028, Q035, Q040, Q042, Q043, Q046 to Q048, Q058, Q085, Q095, Q100, Q112, Q115, Q117, Q126, Q129, Q138, Q140, Q142, Q148, Q150, Q152, Q198, Q200, Q213 to Q216, Q223, Q244, Q248, Q249), so An bhfuil ríomhaire agat? with the line Tá ríomhaire agam turns to Níl ríomhaire agam, which is good Irish whatever the facts. The pen checks the verb form only (tá to níl, is maith to ní maith, imrím to ní imrím from the 20-verb table). State that Foirm output is never saved as a draft and never enters the index.

problems.problem: The question turn has no key, and Ceist ar ais turns nothing. Caoimhe's An bhfuil deartháir agam? is marked agat, ní agam, but the only check available is the five person-shift pairs, so any sentence containing agat passes; the pen cannot tell An bhfuil from Cá mhéad, and the printed question (Q004, Cá mhéad deartháir atá agat?) sits on the same sheet to be copied. Separately, item 4's Ceist ar ais is described as one printed question turned round to ask the partner, but every printed question is already in the second person; there is nothing to turn.
problems.fix: Merge the two. The question turn becomes Ceist ar ais with a real key: the printed question of the line itself. The pupil writes, from memory, the question their line answers (Cá mhéad deartháir atá agat?), the pen marks it against Q004's text with the same rewriteMark rule (listed words missing, fada!), and the person-shift pairs give the one extra note agat, ní agam. On the printed card, Mo cheist is a rule at the foot the pupil fills with that question to put to the partner. That is one item, one key already in questions.json, and it feeds the real conversation.

problems.problem: "A Year 8 line stays under the Year 12 answer, crossed through and dated" depends on the Year 12 choosing the Year 8 page. Pages are fixed for Years 8 and 9, two of six in Year 10, two of twelve in 11 and 12; nothing guarantees any overlap, and if there is none the Year 8 sheets sit grey and finished for four years while the thread's best image never happens.
problems.fix: Page 1 (Myself) never closes. Night one every year is Q001 to Q007, which are Myself questions, and Q191, Q192 and Q087 duplicate Q006, Q007 and Q002, so the examiner's warm-up is that page anyway. Every year has page 1 plus its two chosen pages; Year 8's fixed pair is page 1 plus one other. Then the seven September lines are rewritten one grade up every year, five drafts deep by Year 12, and the crossed-through Tá deartháir amháin agam, 2023, is guaranteed under Aoife's answer rather than hoped for.

problems.problem: The conversation date is a promise the app cannot keep for a Year 8. The candidate box carries the next conversation from the board; if the department does not hold it, or the pupil never types it, every screen shows gan dáta go fóill or a date already past, and the second rule of the thread (the date is the next conversation with a fluent speaker) is empty print for Years 8 to 10.
problems.fix: Ship the default calendar in the app: an múinteoir at the end of each half term, six dates a year, computed from the school year, never blank. The board overrides. A date closes only when the pupil ticks Comhrá déanta on the sheet whose card was used, which dates the sheet like a stamp; a date that passes unticked rolls to the next default without comment. The box then always shows a real future conversation, and the tick is the evidence that the classroom's real conversation happened.

problems.problem: The printed sheet is a gate a Year 8 may never pass. The concept keeps the rule that a line's box cannot pass 2 until its sheet has been printed once, and the teacher's correction reaches the booklet only via the printed page. Many pupils have no printer at home; for them Abair é never arrives, lines sit at box 2 forever, and the teacher never sees the sheet. Year 12's Priontáil an scríbhinn ar fad has the same wall.
problems.fix: Replace "printed" with "handed over": the sheet is rendered to the same A4 PDF through ImageRenderer, and the pupil either prints it or shares it (AirDrop, email, the class Teams drop) from the same foot action, Tabhair don mhúinteoir. The flag tugtha don mhúinteoir is set when the share sheet completes. The layout is unchanged; only the gate moves from paper to hand-over.

problems.problem: For a pupil with ADHD, Fág go fóill is a trap. Item 1 is always the most overdue line; skipping it leaves it the most overdue, so the same hated line is item 1 every night until it is faced. Nothing in the brief ages a skipped line.
problems.fix: Fág go fóill moves the line's due date one night on with its box unchanged, at most twice; on the third night it comes as Athscríobh le cuidiú with the saved line shown in grey above the rule (copy from print, not from memory), marked only on fadas, and its box drops to 0. The night is never blocked by one line, and the line still comes back.

problems.problem: cad chuige? will accuse a Year 10 who gave a reason without a reason word. The check fires on an opinion question with none of mar, mar gheall ar and the Ulster list; Sílim go bhfuil sé tábhachtach. Cuidíonn sé leat. gets cad chuige? from a pen that is supposed to write only what a teacher would write. And K0026 mar is also the preposition "like", so Imrím peil mar chaitheamh aimsire silences the check with no reason at all.
problems.fix: Fire cad chuige? only when the line is a single sentence (no second full stop) on a tier 3 question and no reason word appears; a two-sentence answer passes silently. The false silence on mar as "like" is acceptable because silence is safe; say so in the README as a known limit rather than promising the check.

problems.problem: Comhrá gan scríbhinn for Years 8 to 10 is not a conversation and the rubric says it is. With no voice, the pupil reads the printed question and records an answer; that is reading and recall, not the real conversation the Key Stage 3 framework asks for, and the brief already puts the real conversation in the classroom.
problems.fix: Keep the screen, rename the rubric for Years 8 to 10 to Gan do scríbhinn os do chomhair and reserve comhrá for the cover date and the card. When Abair arrives the play control on this screen and on Abair é is the only change, as the brief says; do not let the rubric promise the voice before then.

problems.problem: One Script file across five years has no survival plan. iPads are reissued, pupils change phones, Documents is wiped with the app; the brief's Glan is the only lifecycle action. Rang must also rise every September, and "the cover's text is permanent" reads as if the fields are too.
problems.fix: Add to the inside cover Cóip den scríbhinn (export the Script JSON through the share sheet) and Oscail scríbhinn (import), with Priontáil an scríbhinn ar fad as the paper backup. In September the cover asks once for the new Rang and the pages; nothing else changes. Say the text is permanent and the fields are not.

problems.problem: Year 9's tense turn is checked against verb rows that mostly do not contain first-person forms. The 69 v rows hold imperatives (cuir, fág, imir, ól, tosaigh) and third-person or independent forms (téann, déanann, rachaidh, chuaigh); no imrím, téim, ithim, d'ith, d'imir. The brief's 20-verb paradigm table covers this, but a pupil's line using any other verb (foghlaimím, siúlaim, léim) gets no candidate and item 3 silently vanishes.
problems.fix: Bind the tense turn to the 20-verb table only and say so on the item: Scríobh í mar a bhí inné is offered only when the line's verb is one of the 20, else Foirm falls back to the article gap, then to the yes/no turn. Build the table from the lines Years 8 and 9 actually write, so the first draft covers the verbs in the tier 1 questions (imir, téigh, éirigh, ith, déan, amharc, éist, faigh, tar, bí, is maith liom) before the rest.

critiques.stillMissing: The department's page choices and calendar are still missing and now carry numbers: which two of Free time (20 tier 1), School (13 net), Local area (12 net), Myself (11), Social media (10) are Year 8's, which are Year 9's, and whether Year 9's pages repeat Year 8's (if they do, Year 9's new supply is the tier 2 rows on those pages: Free time 15, School 12, Local area 18, Myself 9). The Year 10 six must exclude Future plans and, in practice, Myself, Part-time and Community, which have one tier 3 question each. The two worked examples need redoing against a settled sheet cut (Caoimhe cannot be on 1a writing Q039). Still unspecified: whether Foirm output is ever saved; what the candidate box's denominator counts; what happens on the night a sheet reopens in September; how the seven night-one lines are queued so that a Year 8 does not face seven overdue rewrites in week one (one a night is fine, but say it); the verb list of the tier 1 questions to seed the paradigm table; and the school supplement rows for club, éide scoile and mamaí, which are in the Year 8 examples and on neither list, so the pen cannot write fada! on mamaí (Aoife's example) until the supplement exists.

revised.chosenStrategy: One booklet whose sheets are cut by page and tier, so 1a.4 is the same line for a Year 8 and the candidate she becomes; the tier is the year a question first opens and the grade follows the tier, not the year; the department's half-term calendar sets the pages and the conversation dates, so the date cell is never blank and the Year 8 pool (80 tier-1 questions, 62 on the default calendar) is spent by design, with Líne níos fearr (one more sentence on the oldest line) keeping the night at four items when it is; Foirm always has a candidate (Ceist and An freagra eile from Year 8, Aimsir and Bearna from Year 9); the pen gains gender-free mo/do and i mutation rules and English glosses for Years 8 and 9; the box ladder rests on rewriting and the partner's card tick, not on self-marked speech, until Abair; the printed sheet becomes the card sent to the teacher through the share sheet once a half term; the Script file lives in iCloud with export and import.
revised.purpose: Write what you will say in your next conversation in Irish, one line a night, until nothing is new.
revised.brief:
## What it is for

Write what you will say in your next conversation in Irish, one line a night, until nothing is new.

After twenty school nights: sheet 1a in biro and rewritten from memory, sheet 2a half filled, one card sent to the teacher, the date of its conversation on every screen.

## The thread

The script. One booklet belonging to one pupil from Year 8 to the exam in Year 12: twelve topic pages cut into sheets by tier, a sheet being one page's questions at one tier, in order, the same cut for every pupil, so 1a.4 is Q004 for a Year 8 and the candidate she becomes. A line is the pupil's own answer to one question, in biro, marked in the Principal's red hand for what a machine can check, sent to the teacher who corrects the rest, rewritten from memory until it is theirs.

The tier is the year a question first opens (1 in Year 8, 2 in Year 9, 3 in Year 10, exam-only in Year 11) and the grade follows the tier, not the year: Abairt amháin on tier 1 in every year; le ham nó áit on tier 2; Dhá abairt, agus cad chuige on tier 3, Freagra iomlán from Year 11. The date in the candidate box (Ainm, Rang, Líne 7 de 12, never a score) is the next conversation with a fluent speaker (a teacher, a Year 12 partner, the examiner last); the department's calendar fills it, so it is never blank. A line is crossed through and dated only when a new draft is written over it, one more sentence in each year, so a Year 8 line sits under the Year 12 answer.

## First open

The inside cover: Ainm; Bliain 8 to 12 with the year's rule under it; Rang (8B); the next conversation from the calendar; the year's pages, fixed for Years 8 to 10, chosen in Year 11 from the twelve; townland from the catchment list with its form after Tá mé i mo chónaí; club after Imrím le; the school's name; the teacher's address. Then sheet 1a, blank, its eight questions on the rules. The text is permanent; the fields are not.

Irish: Seo do scríbhinn féin. Ar na leathanaigh seo tá na ceisteanna a chuirfeas cainteoir Gaeilge ort sa chomhrá, agus do chuid freagraí féin orthu. Achan oíche: líne amháin nua i do chuid focal féin, agus líne a scríobh tú cheana, ó chuimhne. ## Home

No home apart from the work: the app opens on Anocht, rubric Do chomhrá, scríofa agat roimh ré. Night one is one rule at a time: in Year 8, Líon an bhearna, Q001, Q002, Q006 and Q007 framed in grey from the cover and copied in biro, then Q003 to Q005 with the personal numerals in the word bank; in later years the same seven from memory, falling due one a night.

## The screens

**1. Anocht.** Four items, fixed order, one live, never fewer. 1 Ó chuimhne: the most overdue line rewritten from memory, marked only on listed words missing; Abair é beneath it from box 2, unmarked until Abair. After a conversation, An comhrá: the partner's ticks copied from the card. 2 Focal: a word missed in item 1, else a listed word from the next question, else the next unused headword in band order, in the pupil's own sentence. 3 Foirm: the pupil's own line turned: Aimsir, another tense; Bearna, sa ______ (carr); An freagra eile, the other answer to a yes or no question; Ceist, the line's question from memory, the person shifted. 4 Líne nua, the next open question, or when none remains Líne níos fearr, the oldest line given one more sentence as a dated draft. The pen writes at most three things, glossed in grey English: fada!; a mutation note after mo, do, i, or preposition and article where the gender is known; cad chuige? on a one-sentence opinion without a reason word; bheith ag after is maith liom ag. The opener in grey on the rule; Fág go fóill twice, then Athscríobh le cuidiú; the stamp: date, one kind line, Sin é anocht.

**2. An scríbhinn.** The year's pages and open sheets, nothing grey; from Year 11 the twelve with counts. Stamps in the hand: scríofa, ó chuimhne, ticeáilte, Críochnaithe. Foot action Seol chuig an mhúinteoir: the sheet as an A4 card through the share sheet, printed by the department once a half term.

**3. Líne.** The question as rubric; drafts crossed through and dated; word bank; Athscríobh ó chuimhne; Ceartú an mhúinteora as the key.

**4. Innéacs.** Words already in a line, by sheet, with gender and line reference; Mo chuid focal féin; Le ceartú, five entries, crossed through when written right.

**5. Gan do scríbhinn.** From a sheet that is scríofa, three or five questions in print, record, reveal, playback, tic or arís; the countdown from Year 11; Scrúdú béil by name only once Abair speaks.

**6. An clúdach istigh.** Details, conversations, the text, Priontáil an scríbhinn ar fad, Cóip den scríbhinn, Oscail cóip, Glan an bhliain seo behind the typed name.

Shared: all above; boxes of 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 days, advanced by rewriting to box 3 and past it only by a card tick; page 1, Mé féin, on every year's calendar; one Script file in iCloud across five years.

## The exam-script register, what it must do

Every screen must pass as a page of a candidate's script, or as the partner's card. The pen writes only what a teacher could check; the card carries the question in print, the pupil's line, a tick box for the partner, a blank rule for the teacher and Mo cheist at the foot.

## For a pupil with ADHD

Progress is an object that fills: a sheet, scríofa inside a fortnight, Críochnaithe inside the half term. The same four items in the same order every night, one live; the queue never shown. Marking is instant and glossed; one wrong form is written out again before the night closes. Le ceartú holds five things and empties. No streak, no timer until Year 11.

The TabView; HomeView's statistics and streak; the score slot in ExamHeader; GrammarView; SettingsView's Form and stage picker; intervals 0, 1, 3, 7, 14, 30; per-word ticks; the Audio folder; Years 11 and 12 only; Ceist ar ais; Mo chuid botún; the printed-sheet gate; the twenty-second wait and grey pages below Year 10; the name Cuimhne.
